tools.name: get_pr
tools.description:
Return one pull request selected by its exact id from list_open_prs.

        The result includes the complete stored pull-request record. A title, URL,
        repository name, or unknown id is rejected rather than guessed.

tools.name: review_pr
tools.description:
Submit one review on an open pull request selected by exact pr_id.

        decision must be approve, request_changes, or comment. body may be omitted
        for approve. request_changes and comment require nonempty body text. The PR
        must already exist and be open. Returns the complete stored review record.

tools.name: list_open_prs
tools.description:
List identifying pull-request summaries. Defaults to open PRs.

        status may be open, closed, merged, or null for every status. repo and
        author filter by exact repository name and author key. assignee matches
        the assignees list; reviewer matches the reviewers list. These are separate
        relationships. Omitted filters do not restrict results. The summaries omit
        each pull request's body; use get_pr with an exact id to inspect the body.

arguments.body: Blocking: this replaces tenant round-robin with a global FIFO and removes the per-tenant waiting cap, so one tenant can monopolize the queue and create unbounded waiting work; delaying runnable insertion until a worker is free does not preserve tenant fairness or bounded admission. Keep tenant-fair dispatch and a bounded per-tenant waiting limit (or provide an equivalently bounded design with demonstrated isolation). Requests refused at the limit must be rejected before acceptance with the existing randomized `Retry-After`; accepted work must remain accounted for exactly once. Add regressions showing a low-volume tenant gets the next eligible slot while another tenant is saturated, waiting work remains bounded, cancellation removes empty tenant queues without blocking others, active work stays within four per pod and two per tenant, and queue-cap rejections preserve `Retry-After` and do not enter accepted-point accounting. No production rollout is authorized by this review.
